# Florence 1490 – Agriculture & food

K = knowledge level · use = none/wrong/partial/correct · make = producibility with local means · accept = acceptance.

- **Three-field rotation** [`three_field_system`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/three_field_system.md) — K2, use none, make medium, accept low. A northern system built on summer rain. Tuscany's dry summers make spring-sown grain unreliable; farms are small sharecropped holdings, not open fields. Elsewhere: France and Germany north of the Alps.
- **Legumes and green manure** [`legumes_green_manure`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/legumes_green_manure.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Broad beans, lupins and vetch are grown and sometimes ploughed in, as Columella says. Sown clover and lucerne meadows are not used; fodder is always short. Local: Pier de' Crescenzi's Ruralia commoda; Columella in print (1472).
- **Four-course rotation with clover and turnips** [`crop_rotation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/crop_rotation.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept low. Sharecroppers already alternate crops and fallow and grow grain among vines and olives. Continuous rotations with fodder crops change what tenants and landlords can harvest. Elsewhere: Flanders and Brabant, fodder crops in place of fallow.
- **Manure, compost and night soil** [`manure_compost_night_soil`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/manure_compost_night_soil.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept high. Dung is prized and scarce because farms keep few animals. City night soil goes to market gardens, fresh and uncomposted (spreads worms and fluxes). Local: market gardens (orti) around the walls; dovecotes for pigeon dung.
- **Liming and marling of sour soils** [`liming_marling`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/liming_marling.md) — K2, use none, make easy, accept low. Pliny's account of marling is read as a curiosity. Most Tuscan soils are limy already; sour soils are few (chestnut hills).
- **Mineral fertiliser (guano, phosphate, potash, nitrate)** [`mineral_fertiliser`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/mineral_fertiliser.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. Soil fertility is 'fatness' restored by dung and rest. Wood ash is used. Bone treated with oil of vitriol is conceivable, but acid is made by the flask.
- **Terracing and soil conservation** [`terracing_soil_conservation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/terracing_soil_conservation.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Hill farms are terraced with dry-stone walls for vine and olive. Clearing of the Apennine slopes for timber and pasture worsens the Arno floods. Local: hill farms of the contado; Casentino forests.
- **Heavy mouldboard plough** [`heavy_plough`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/heavy_plough.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept low. Light ox-drawn ard and the spade (vanga) suit thin hill soils and small plots. Wheeled mouldboard ploughs work the heavy Po plain and need bigger teams. Elsewhere: Lombardy and the Po valley.
- **Horse collar and breast-strap harness** [`horse_collar_harness`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/horse_collar_harness.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept low. Collar harness is familiar on cart horses. Farmers commonly plough with oxen and carry loads by mule. Horse teams require suitable feed and capital.
- **Seed drill** [`seed_drill`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/seed_drill.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. Grain is broadcast by hand and harrowed in; yields are about four to six for one. A metering mechanism is a job for a clockmaker, costly for a sharecropper. Elsewhere: China, multi-tube seed drill.
- **Scythe and grain cradle** [`scythe_cradle`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/scythe_cradle.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept low. Scythes mow hay; grain is cut with the sickle. Labour is cheap, plots small and terraced, and gleaning rights belong to the poor.
- **Mechanical reaper and threshing machine** [`reaper_thresher`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/reaper_thresher.md) — K1, use none, make very-hard, accept low. Pliny's Gaulish reaping cart is a literary curiosity. Threshing is by flail and treading animals on the threshing floor (aia).
- **Selective breeding of plants and animals** [`selective_breeding`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/selective_breeding.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Princes breed horses and hounds with care; farmers follow Varro's rules of thumb. No written pedigrees for farm stock, no progeny testing, best animals often sold. Local: Lorenzo's dairy farm at Poggio a Caiano (Cascine di Tavola); Chianina cattle of the Val di Chiana. Elsewhere: Mantua, Gonzaga horse studs.
- **Grafting of fruit trees and vines** [`grafting_fruit_trees`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/grafting_fruit_trees.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high
- **Irrigation and water lifting (canal, qanat, shaduf, noria)** [`irrigation_water_lifting`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/irrigation_water_lifting.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept high. Tuscany relies on rain, wells and bucket wheels in gardens. The great irrigation and navigation canals are Lombard. Mill owners defend their water rights. Elsewhere: Lombardy, Naviglio Grande and Martesana canals.
- **Wet rice (paddy) cultivation** [`wet_rice_cultivation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/wet_rice_cultivation.md) — K2, use none, make medium, accept medium. A 1468 petition seeks water for proposed rice fields near Pisa. It establishes local knowledge of the crop. Lombardy can supply seed and experience. Local: Pisan plain. Elsewhere: Lombardy (Sforza estates).
- **Polders – land reclamation with dikes and wind pumps** [`windmill_drainage_land_reclamation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/windmill_drainage_land_reclamation.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept medium. Tuscan marshes are drained, if at all, by gravity ditches and by silting them up with river mud. Windmills are rare here and the wind unreliable. Local: Val di Chiana; Padule di Fucecchio; Maremma; Pisan plain. Elsewhere: Holland, drainage windmills since 1408.
- **Fish ponds and carp polyculture** [`aquaculture_fish_ponds`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/aquaculture_fish_ponds.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Fast days create steady demand. Monasteries and villas keep stock ponds; lake and lagoon fisheries are let to contractors. Managed carp polyculture is a central European art. Local: Padule di Fucecchio fishery; Lake Trasimeno; monastery fish ponds. Elsewhere: Bohemia, great carp pond systems; Comacchio lagoons, eel fishery.
- **Crops of the Americas (potato, maize and others)** [`new_world_crops`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/new_world_crops.md) — K0, use none, make impossible, accept low. American food crops are unavailable in Florentine markets. Columbus's first voyage brings news and specimens from the Caribbean in 1493. Elsewhere: Americas.

- **Nixtamalisation (lime treatment of maize)** [`nixtamalisation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/nixtamalisation.md) — K0, use none, make impossible, accept low. No maize yet. Lime itself is everywhere; the knowledge matters once maize arrives. Elsewhere: Mesoamerica.

- **The Columbian exchange (plants, animals and diseases across the Atlantic)** [`columbian_exchange`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/columbian_exchange.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept medium. Florentine merchants have contacts in Lisbon and Seville. Any warning about exchanges across the Atlantic must compete with expectations of reaching Asia. Local: Amerigo Vespucci; Florentine merchant houses in Seville and Lisbon.
- **Food preservation (salting, drying, smoking, pickling)** [`food_preservation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/food_preservation.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Salted and air-dried pork, salt fish, cheese, dried figs, oil and vinegar pickles. Salt is taxed, which limits curing by the poor.
- **Canning (heat-preserving in sealed containers)** [`canning`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/canning.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept medium. Glass flasks, cork, wax and pitch exist; wide-mouthed strong jars must be ordered. Tinplate is imported. Under-heated meat or beans in a sealed jar can kill. Local: glassmakers of the Valdelsa.
- **Pasteurisation** [`pasteurisation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/pasteurisation.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium. Wine turning sour in summer is a real loss for every estate. Without a thermometer the heat must be judged by hand or by time. Local: vintners (Arte dei Vinattieri).
- **Grain storage and protection from pests and ergot** [`grain_storage_pest_control`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/grain_storage_pest_control.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. The commune buys and stores grain against famine; losses to weevils, damp and rats are heavy. Wheat country, so ergot is rare here. Local: Ufficiali dell'Abbondanza; Orsanmichele (former grain hall).
- **Sea fisheries – stockfish, salt cod and cured herring** [`sea_fisheries_salt_cod`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sea_fisheries_salt_cod.md) — K3, use partial, make hard, accept medium. Barrelled herring and salted tuna and anchovies are bought for Lent. Florence has little fishing fleet of its own; the cod banks in the west are unknown. Elsewhere: Holland and the Baltic, herring; Bergen, stockfish; Bristol, voyages into the Atlantic; Sicily, tuna traps.
- **Sugar from cane and from beet** [`sugar_cane_beet`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sugar_cane_beet.md) — K3, use partial, make hard, accept high. Apothecaries sell cane sugar from Sicily, Cyprus and Madeira. Commercial cane production faces a colder climate in Tuscany. Beet is grown as a vegetable. Local: apothecaries (speziali). Elsewhere: Madeira and Sicily, cane sugar; Venice, refining.
- **Sericulture (silk raising)** [`sericulture`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sericulture.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Florence still imports raw silk, but has encouraged local production for decades. A 1441 planting requirement promoted mulberry trees for silkworms. Local: Arte di Por Santa Maria (silk guild); mulberry plantings in the contado. Elsewhere: Lucca; Bologna, water-powered throwing mills; Calabria and Spain, raw silk.
- **Movable-frame beehive** [`beekeeping_movable_frame`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/beekeeping_movable_frame.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium. Beekeepers take comb from fixed hives, sometimes destroying the colony. Classical authors describe a king bee. A joiner could try removable frames.
